NONE: › to separate or remove something from something else that it is connected to
使分離，使分開；拆掉

example: You can detach the hood if you prefer the coat without it.
如果不想要大衣上的帽兜，可以拆掉。
Detach the lower part of the form from this letter and return it to the above address.
請將表格的下半部分從信中剪下來，並寄到上述地址。

NONE: › able to be detached
可拆下的；可分離的，可分開的

example: a detachable collar/hood
可拆下來的衣領／帽兜

NONE: › separated
分離的，分開的；拆下的
C1 UK A detached house is not connected to any other building.
（房子）獨幢的，獨立的
C2 A detached person does not show any emotional involvement or interest in a situation.
認為與己無關的；毫不關心的，心不在焉的

example: The label became detached from your parcel.
標籤已經從你的包裹上掉下來了。
Prices are rising so fast that people can't afford detached houses.
房價上漲得如此之快，人們已經買不起獨立屋了。
Compare
semi-detached
She seemed a bit detached, as if her mind were on other things.
她似乎有些心不在焉，好像心思在別的事情上。
Throughout the novel, the story is seen through the eyes of a detached observer.
整部小說的故事情節都是從一個旁觀者的角度展開的。

C, + sing/pl verb: › [ C,  + sing/pl verb ] a group of soldiers who are separated from the main group in order to perform a particular duty

U: › [ U ] a feeling of not being emotionally involved

example: a military detachment
軍事行動小組
A detachment of Italian soldiers was sent to the area.
一支由義大利士兵組成的小分隊被派往了該地區。
to have an air of detachment
一副事不關己的樣子

C: B1 [ C ] a single piece of information or fact about something
A2 information about someone or something

U: › [ U ] the small features of something that you only notice when you look carefully
B1 including or considering all the information about something or every part of something
B2 to tell or include all the facts about something
C: › [ C ] a part of something that does not seem important
細枝末節，無足輕重的小事

C, + sing/pl verb: › [ C,  + sing/pl verb ] a group of people who have been given a particular task

T: › [ T ] to describe something completely, giving all the facts

T + to infinitive, often passive: › [ T + to infinitive,  often passive ] to order someone, often a small group of soldiers or workers, to perform a particular task

example: She insisted on telling me every single detail of what they did to her in hospital.
她堅持要告訴我她在醫院遭遇的一切。
We don't know the full/precise details of the story yet.
我們還不知道故事的全部／具體情節。
She refused to disclose/divulge any details about/of the plan.
她拒絕透露該計劃的任何細節。
A police officer took down the details of what happened.
一位警官詳細記下了發生的一切。
UK Can I have your details (= name and address, etc.), please?
可以告訴我你的個人詳細情況嗎？
I was just admiring the detail in the doll's house - even the tins of food have labels on them.
我只是感嘆娃娃屋的製作之精緻——就連食品罐頭上都還貼著標籤呢。
It's his eye for (= ability to notice) detail that distinguishes him as a painter.
他細緻入微的觀察能力使其成為一位與眾不同的畫家。
We haven't discussed the matter in detail yet.
我們還沒有詳細討論此事。
The book described her suffering in graphic detail.
這本書詳盡地描述了她所遭受的種種痛苦。
He talked in great detail about the furniture he's chosen for the living room.
他詳細介紹了他為客廳選定的傢俱。
I won't go into detail over the phone, but I've been having a few health problems recently.
我在電話裡就不細說了，但最近我的身體一直有些不舒服。
Tony says, he's going to get the car, and finding the money to pay for it is just a minor detail.
托尼說，他要買那輛車，買車錢不過是小事一樁。
[ + question word ] Can you produce a report detailing what we've spent on the project so far?
你能不能寫一份報告，詳細列出到目前為止我們在這個企劃案上的花費？
Four soldiers were detailed to check the road for troops.
派出了四名士兵為部隊檢查道路情況。

NONE: B2 giving a lot of information with many details
詳盡的，詳細的

example: A witness gave a detailed description of the man.
一位目擊者詳細描述了那個人的體貌特徵。

NONE: › to force someone officially to stay in a place
使留下；拘留，扣押
› to delay someone for a short length of time
（短時間地）耽擱，拖延
› to keep someone in prison for as long as the courts feel is necessary
無限期關押（某人）

example: A suspect has been detained by the police for questioning.
一名嫌疑人已被員警拘留接受進一步審訊。
Several of the injured were detained overnight in hospital.
傷者中有幾個人被留院觀察了一晚。
I'm sorry I'm late - I was unavoidably detained.
對不起我來晚了——沒辦法我被耽擱了一會兒。

NONE: › a person who has been officially ordered to stay in a prison or similar place, especially for political reasons
（尤指因政治原因的）被拘留者，被關押者

example: a political detainee
政治犯

NONE: C1 to notice something that is partly hidden or not clear, or to discover something, especially using a special method
（尤指用特殊方法）發現，察覺，看出
C1 to discover something, usually using special equipment
（通常指用特別設備）探測，檢測，測出

example: Some sounds cannot be detected by the human ear.
有些聲音是人的耳朵無法察覺到的。
Financial experts have detected signs that the economy is beginning to improve.
金融專家已經注意到經濟開始有好轉的跡象。
High levels of lead were detected in the atmosphere.
經檢測發現大氣中鉛的含量很高。
Radar equipment is used to detect (= find the position of) enemy aircraft.
雷達裝置用於探測敵機的位置。

NONE: › the fact of noticing or discovering something
察覺；發現
› the fact of the police discovering information about crimes
偵破（案件）

example: Early detection of the cancer improves the chances of successful treatment.
及早發現癌症能提高治癒的機率。
bomb detection
炸彈探測
a low/high crime detection rate
低／高破案率

NONE: B1 someone whose job is to discover information about crimes and find out who is responsible for them
偵探
› used as part of the title of particular ranks in the police force
警探（用於某些級別的員警頭銜）

example: a private detective
私家偵探
Detective Sergeant Lewis
路易士探長

NONE: › the activity of searching for information about something, often over a long period
調查，查找，搜尋

example: After a lot of detective work, I managed to find out where he was living.
經過大量的調查，我終於設法找到了他的住處。

NONE: › a device used to find particular substances or things, or measure their level
探測器；測量器

example: a metal/smoke detector
金屬／煙霧探測器

NONE: › an improvement in the relationship between two countries that in the past were not friendly and did not trust each other
（國家間關係的）緩和，緩解

example: The talks are aimed at furthering détente between the two countries.
會談旨在進一步緩和兩國間的關係。

U: › [ U ] the act of officially detaining someone
C or U: › [ C or U ] a form of punishment in which children are made to stay at school for a short time after classes have ended

example: Concern has been expressed about the death in detention of a number of political prisoners.
人們對一些政治犯在關押期間死去表示關注。
She's had four detentions this term.
這學期她四次被罰留堂。

NONE: › a type of prison where young people can be kept for short periods of time
（青少年）管教所，教養所
› a place where people who have entered a country without the necessary documents can be kept for short periods of time
（非法移民）拘留所
› Indian English for
detainee
› to prevent someone from doing something or to make someone less enthusiastic about doing something by making it difficult for that person to do it or by threatening bad results if they do it
阻撓，阻止；威懾；使不敢

example: These measures are designed to deter an enemy attack.
這些措施旨在阻止敵人的進攻。
High prices are deterring many young people from buying houses.
高昂的價格讓很多年輕人對於買房屋望而卻步。

NONE: › a chemical substance in the form of a powder or a liquid for removing dirt from clothes, dishes, etc.
洗衣粉；洗衣液；清潔劑
C1 to become worse
惡化，變壞

example: She was taken into hospital last week when her condition suddenly deteriorated.
她是在上周病情突然惡化時被送進醫院的。
The political situation in the region has deteriorated rapidly.
該地區的政治形勢已急劇惡化。

NONE: › formal something that controls or affects what happens in a particular situation
決定因素

example: Soil and climate are the main determinants of how land is used.
土壤和氣候是土地使用形式的決定因素。

NONE: › fixed or exact
限定的；確定的，明確的

example: A determinate sentence of imprisonment was imposed.
明確判決有期徒刑。
Compare
indeterminate

U: B2 [ U ] the ability to continue trying to do something, although it is very difficult
› [ U ] formal the process of controlling, influencing, or deciding something

C or U: › [ C or U ] formal the process of finding something out

example: a man of fierce/ruthless determination
很有毅力／痛下決心的人
[ + to infinitive ] You can't help but admire her determination to succeed.
她有很大的決心獲得成功，這一點讓人非常欽佩。
See also
self-determination
The determination of policy is not your business - your job is to implement it.
政策的決定與你無關——你的工作就是執行。
the determination of his whereabouts
查明他的下落

T often passive: C1 [ T often passive ] to control or influence something directly, or to decide what will happen
T: › [ T ] formal to make a strong decision
C1 [ T ] formal to discover the facts or truth about something

example: The number of staff we can take on will be determined by how much money we're allowed to spend.
我們僱用的人數將取決於可支配資金的多少。
Your health is determined in part by what you eat.
在某種程度上你的健康狀況取決於你的飲食。
Eye colour is genetically determined.
眼睛的顏色是由遺傳基因決定的。
[ + question word ] formal Officials will determine whether or not the game will be played.
官員將決定這場比賽能否進行。
People should be allowed to determine their own future.
應該允許人們決定自己的未來。
[ + that ] She determined that one day she would be an actor.
她決心將來當演員。
[ + to infinitive ] On leaving jail, Joe determined to reform.
祖出獄後決心改過自新。
The police never actually determined the cause of death.
警方實際上從未查明死因。
[ + question word ] It is the responsibility of the court to determine whether these men are innocent.
確定這些人是否無辜是法庭的責任。
[ + that ] The jury determined that the men were guilty.
陪審團裁決那些人有罪。

NONE: B2 wanting to do something very much and not allowing anyone or any difficulties to stop you
下定決心的，堅決的，決意的

example: [ + to infinitive ] I'm determined to get this piece of work done today.
我決心今天完成這項工作。
She will get the job she wants - she's a very determined person.
她肯定會得到她想要的那份工作——她是個意志很堅定的人。

NONE: B2 in grammar, a word that is used before a noun to show which particular example of the noun you are referring to
限定詞

example: In the phrases "my first boyfriend" and "that strange woman", the words "my" and "that" are determiners.
在 my first boyfriend 和 that strange woman 這兩個片語中，my 和 that 都是限定詞。

NONE: › the theory that everything that happens must happen as it does and could not have happened any other way
決定論（認為一切事物具有不以人的意志為轉移的必然性）
› relating to the theory that everything that happens must happen as it does and could not have happened any other way
決定論的（認為一切事物具有不以人的意志為轉移的必然性）

example: the determinist hypothesis
決定論假說

NONE: › believing that everything that happens must happen as it does and could not have happened any other way, or relating to this belief
決定論（者）的（認為一切事物具有不以人的意志為轉移的必然性）

example: It would be overly deterministic to say that if the party did change its leader, the new one would continue to make the same mistakes.
有人認為如果該政黨改換領袖，新的領導人將會繼續重複同樣的錯誤，這樣的看法實在是決定論者的論調。

NONE: › the action or the fact of deterring people from doing something
威懾；遏制；制止

example: They believed in the principle of nuclear deterrence.
他們相信核武器的威懾力。

NONE: C2 something that deters people from doing something
威懾力量；遏制因素；制止物

example: a nuclear deterrent
核威懾力
Tougher prison sentences may act/serve as a deterrent to other would-be offenders.
從嚴判決可以起到震懾其他潛在犯罪者的作用。

NONE: › to hate someone or something very much
憎恨；厭惡，討厭

example: I detest any kind of cruelty.
我厭惡任何形式的殘暴。
[ + -ing verb ] I detest having to get up when it's dark outside.
我討厭天還未亮就要起床。
her detested older brother
她那令人討厭的哥哥

NONE: › used to refer to people or things that you hate very much
可憎的，可惡的，令人厭惡的

example: a detestable coward
可惡的膽小鬼

NONE: › to remove a king or queen from their position of power
廢黜，推翻（國王或女王）；使下臺
› to beat someone who is the best at something, especially a sport, and become the best yourself
（尤指在體育比賽中）打敗，擊敗（頂尖好手）

example: The world champion was dethroned by a young Swedish challenger.
那位世界冠軍被一名年輕的瑞典挑戰者擊敗。

NONE: › to (cause something to) explode
引爆，（使）爆炸

example: The device detonated unexpectedly.
裝置發生了意外爆炸。
A remote control device was used to detonate the bomb.
有人用遙控裝置引爆了那枚炸彈。

NONE: › the act of exploding something, or the fact of being exploded
引爆，起爆

example: Underground nuclear detonations are believed to have been carried out.
據信已經進行了地下核引爆。

NONE: › a small amount of explosive in a bomb that explodes first and causes a larger explosion, or an electrical device that is used from a distance to make a bomb explode
起爆劑；起爆器
› a different or less direct route to a place that is used to avoid a problem or to visit somewhere or do something on the way
繞行的路，迂回路
› US UK diversion a different route that is used because a road is closed
繞行路線

example: Traffic detours will be kept to a minimum throughout the festival.
在節日期間，儘量不實行交通繞行措施。

NONE: › a period when you stop taking unhealthy or harmful foods, drinks, or drugs into your body for a period of time, in order to improve your health
（為改善健康而）停止食用（不健康或有害食物的）一段時間；（酒癮或毒癮的）戒除期
› medical treatment in a special hospital to stop someone drinking too much alcohol or taking harmful drugs
戒酒治療；戒毒治療
› to stop taking unhealthy or harmful foods, drinks, and other substances into your body for a period of time, in order to improve your health
停止食用（不健康或有害食物）；戒除（酒癮等）
› to have medical treatment in a special hospital in order to stop drinking too much alcohol or taking harmful drugs
（使）戒去酒癮；（使）戒去毒癮

example: She went on a 48-hour detox, eating nothing but grapes.
她進行了48小時的節食，期間只吃葡萄，別的甚麼都不吃。
a detox diet
節制性飲食
He'd spent 18 months in detox/at a detox centre fighting drug addiction.
他在戒毒中心與毒癮抗爭了18個月。
If you have skin problems or feel sluggish and run-down, then it may be time to detox.
如果你患有皮膚病或感到懶散乏力，那麼就該在飲食上有所注意了。

NONE: › the process of removing harmful chemicals from something
解毒，去毒
› a place similar to a hospital where people go to receive treatment for drinking too much alcohol or taking too many drugs
戒毒中心；戒酒中心
› to make something seem less valuable or less deserving of admiration than it really is
（在價值、美譽等方面）對…產生不利影響；眨低；有損乎

example: All that make-up she wears actually detracts from her beauty, I think.
我認為她的那種化妝效果實際上有損她的美。

NONE: › someone who criticizes something or someone, often unfairly
惡意批評者，貶低者

example: His detractors claim that his fierce temper makes him unsuitable for leadership.
他的批評者聲稱他脾氣暴躁，不適合做領袖。

NONE: › harm or damage
危害，損害

example: Are you sure that I can follow this diet without detriment to my health?
你能肯定我遵循這樣的飲食不會對健康有害嗎？
She was very involved with sports at college, to the detriment of (= harming) her studies.
她上大學時熱衷於參加體育運動，甚至還因此影響了學業。

NONE: C2 causing harm or damage
有危害的，有損害的

example: These chemicals have a detrimental effect/impact on the environment.
這些化學品對環境有危害。
Their decision could be detrimental to the future of the company.
他們的決定可能會對公司的未來產生不利影響。

NONE: › formal waste material or rubbish, especially left after a particular event
（尤指某項活動後留下的）廢棄物，垃圾
› specialized biology a loose mass of decaying material
風化物；岩屑

example: The stadium was littered with the detritus of yesterday's concert.
體育館裡到處都是昨天舉行音樂會後留下的垃圾。

NONE: › the muscle that controls the emptying of the bladder (= the organ where urine is stored)
逼尿肌

example: Most incontinent women have either genuine stress incontinence or detrusor instability.
大多數罹患尿失禁的女性要麼是腹部壓迫性尿失禁，要麼是逼尿肌功能失調。
